name: Siari, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve
insider_take: Siari — meaning "happiness" in the indigenous Huichol language — is one of only a handful of Ritz-Carlton Reserve properties on the planet, placing it in an ultra-exclusive tier of experiential luxury set against the wild, lush beauty of Mexico's Pacific coastline.
whats_special: Siari sits within a protected coastal reserve in Riviera Nayarit, where the Sierra Madre mountains dramatically meet the Pacific Ocean. Each villa is a private sanctuary with plunge pools and sweeping jungle or ocean views. Unlike traditional resorts, the Reserve model means ultra-limited guest capacity, deeply personal service, and immersive cultural programming rooted in the ancient traditions of the Huichol people — one of Mexico's most spiritually rich indigenous cultures. The resort's design is organically woven into the landscape, featuring open-air architecture, handcrafted artisan details, and an adults-only atmosphere of serene exclusivity.
pro_tip: Request a Huichol cultural experience at booking — the resort offers rare, intimate encounters with local artisans whose beadwork and yarn art are recognized as UNESCO-level cultural heritage. These sessions book quickly and are not to be missed.
dont_miss: The surrounding Riviera Nayarit coastline offers world-class sport fishing, whale watching (December–March), and the charming cobblestone streets of nearby Sayulita and San Pancho villages. On property, surrender to the Reserve Spa, which incorporates traditional Huichol healing rituals and local botanical ingredients for a wellness experience found nowhere else on earth.
pros: Ultra-exclusive Ritz-Carlton Reserve designation with only a handful of locations worldwide, ensuring an unrivaled level of privacy and personalized service
Breathtaking jungle-meets-ocean setting in Riviera Nayarit, with lush tropical surroundings and direct access to pristine Pacific coastline
Spacious private villa-style accommodations featuring personal plunge pools, open-air terraces, and seamless indoor-outdoor living
World-class culinary experiences showcasing locally sourced Mexican ingredients and Pacific coastal cuisine across multiple dining venues
Immersive wellness and spa offerings inspired by indigenous Huichol traditions and the natural environment of the Sierra Madre mountains
cons: Secluded location requires travel from Puerto Vallarta airport, making it less convenient for quick getaways
Ultra-luxury Reserve pricing places this property at the very top of the rate spectrum, best suited for special occasion travelers
Adults-oriented atmosphere and intimate scale may not be ideal for families with young children seeking resort-style amenities
